key: Speak unto the children of Israel, saying: In the seventh month, in the first day of the month, shall be a solemn rest unto you, a memorial proclaimed with the blast of horns, a holy convocation.
s: Among the seasons appointed through Moses, this one follows Passover and the seven weeks; Rashi, on Leviticus 23:24, reads the memorial as verses of remembrance and of the horn that recall the binding of Isaac, and Ramban, on the same verse, as the blast itself, a remembrance before God on the day He judges, before ten days of pardon.

evidence.words: זכרון תרועה. זִכְרוֹן פְּסוּקֵי זִכְרוֹנוֹת וּפְסוּקֵי שׁוֹפָרוֹת (ספרא: ראש השנה ל"ב) לִזְכֹּר לָכֶם עֲקֵדַת יִצְחָק שֶׁקָּרַב תַּחְתָּיו אַיִל … אבל כל זה אסמכתא מדבריהם … אבל "זכרון תרועה" כמו יום תרועה יהיה לכם (במדבר כט א) יאמר שנריע ביום הזה ויהיה לנו לזכרון לפני השם … מפני שהוא בחדשו של יום הכפורים בראש החודש נראה שבו יהיה דין לפניו יתברך כי בם ידין עמים בראש השנה ישב לכסא שופט צדק ואחרי כן בעשרת הימים ישא לפשע עבדיו
evidence.gloss: [Rashi] A memorial of blasts: a remembrance by the verses of remembrances and the verses of the horn (Sifra; Rosh Hashanah 32), to remember for your sake the binding of Isaac, in whose place a ram was offered. [Ramban] But all this is a scriptural support for their own enactment. But a memorial of blasts is like a day of blasts unto you (Numbers 29:1): we sound the blast on this day and it becomes a remembrance for us before God. Since it falls at the new moon of the month of the day of atonement, it appears that judgement is before Him on it: on the new year He sits on the throne of righteous judgement, and afterwards, in the ten days, He pardons the transgression of His servants.

reason: Key line verbatim (verse.js ok, ref Leviticus 23:24, at [112,24], no also); it is the Torah verse that names and appoints the first day of the seventh month, so it bears directly on the entry. Plain sense checked against Leviticus 23 (tanakh day 39): the chapter lists the LORD's appointed seasons through Moses, Passover, unleavened bread, the sheaf and the count of seven weeks, then this day; no four-word run from the line. In the packet for 23:24 Rashi reads zikhron teruah as the recitation of the remembrance and shofar verses that recall the binding of Isaac; Ramban quotes Rashi, calls this a rabbinic support, reads the memorial as the blast itself being a remembrance before God, and, because the day opens the month of the day of atonement, judges it a day of judgement followed by pardon in the ten days. The two genuinely differ (Ramban names the difference) and the sentence names both without resolving. All four evidence pieces machine-found in the packet; entry-check ok with no warnings. Sforno and Leviticus Rabbah 29:3 also read the day as judgement, consistent with the reading.
